audit.why: Difficulty 4/10 FAVOURED matches the 58.12% win rate over 733 games; Fizz owns every lane stage and Azir's threat is teamfight-side, not lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid-game text invented a '4-second cast animation' on Conquering Sands and gave Nimble Fighter tenacity it does not have.
audit.why: Riot's text for Azir Q is a soldier-thrust with a 1-second slow, no 4s cast; Fizz passive is unit-walking plus flat damage reduction, not tenacity.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown of levels 6-11 around Nimble Fighter's unit-walking and Playful/Trickster's untargetable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shifting Sands was described only as 'his CC' / 'his answer spell' with no cooldown and no statement of what it actually does.
audit.why: Shifting Sands (E) is a shielded dash to a Sand Soldier on 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 — it is Azir's only escape from an all-in, and Fizz's grounding on Playful/Trickster and the knockup on Chum the Waters are the tools that answer it.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now carries the real 22s-to-16s numbers and the 120s ultimate; enemyWin names Arise!, Shifting Sands and Emperor's Divide.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] claimed Chum the Waters deals true damage.
audit.why: Riot's text: the shark knocks up and slows and deals magic damage. No true damage anywhere in Fizz's kit.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - E Playful / Trickster spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands (E): 22s at rank 1, down to 16s at rank 5 — his shield-dash to a soldier. Step up the moment it is spent. - Playful/Trickster burned on poke leaves you 16s with no dodge at rank 1. - Hold Chum the Waters' 120s for a kill, not for poke.

edits.before: Q through him, W bleed, walk out through the wave — the fish phases in and out before his answer finds a target.
edits.after: Bait Shifting Sands with a fake step-in, then commit — his 22-second escape is gone and Urchin Strike closes the gap.

edits.before: Azir burns Shifting Sands on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Azir burns Shifting Sands on a wave — 16 to 22 seconds with no escape.

edits.before: Hopping in first against a held CC — the pole spent as an entrance is the whole kit spent as a coin flip.
edits.after: Pre-6 you have no shark to finish; he dashes out on Shifting Sands and his soldiers chip you all the way back.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Azir wins by walling you out with Arise! soldiers, escaping your commit on Shifting Sands, and Emperor's Divide on your entry.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — shark, string, pole, repeat; one carry per fight is the contract and the pole notarizes it.
edits.after: Carry by deleting Azir himself — he has one escape on a 16s cooldown, so shark him the moment Shifting Sands is spent.

edits.before: Levels 6-11 you keep the pressure on: your all-in combo (E-Q-AA-W) kills faster than he can spend Conquering Sands' 4-second cast animation to peel, and Nimble Fighter's tenacity plus terrain-hop lets you dodge shuffle punishment entirely. He's forced to play passive and shove for tempo instead of contesting you directly.
edits.after: Levels 6-11 you keep the pressure on: your all-in combo (E-Q-AA-W) kills faster than Conquering Sands can peel, and Nimble Fighter's unit-walking plus Playful/Trickster's untargetable window lets you sit out his soldier damage. He's forced to play passive and shove for tempo instead of contesting you directly.

edits.before: Ult removes his kiting angle entirely by putting you point-blank with true damage on the way out
edits.after: Ult removes his kiting angle entirely by sticking a slow on him, then a knockup he cannot dash out of

notes: Level chart left untouched: packet levelChart is Fizz on all seven rows, page agrees on both layers, and 58.12% over 733 games supports it. Suspect name 'Nimble Fighter's' is a false positive on the passive's real name, but the sentence around it (tenacity) was wrong and is fixed. Fizz E grounding vs Azir E dash is plausible but Riot's text does not state that grounding blocks Shifting Sands specifically, so it was not asserted anywhere.
